_comment: How eager NPCs are. NPCs always look after their bodies; everything else they do much less than the player, and politics only when they are unhappy. Raise numbers for livelier NPCs.

asking._comment: When someone asks an NPC for items (or offers a trade worth less than what they want), the NPC may give the unpaid part out of goodwill. Chance = (base + compassion x 'compassion' - ambition x 'ambition') x, for each item asked for, ('all_of_it' + (1 - 'all_of_it') x (1 - asked/have) ^ 'curve') x (1 - 'own_need' x how badly they need it themselves, for food and water). So 1 of their 10 is easy to get, all of it rarely.

_distress_comment: 'distress_damping': a hungry, thirsty, cold or exhausted NPC is this much less keen on anything but looking after themselves (x how urgent their worst need is), except work that brings back what they lack.

discontent._comment: A satisfaction meter below 'starts_below' makes people restless; at 'full_at' fully so. For politics against those in charge, they act on it only once their patience runs out (society.json 'satisfaction.patience').

turnout._comment: Chance an NPC bothers to vote on a ballot: base + discontent bonus + ambition bonus.

appoint._comment: Appointers act when a quality fed by the job is below 'gap_below', at most once every 'days_between' days. 'reassign_reluctance': how much less they like taking someone off other work (it makes them resent it, society.json 'job_loss'). 'store_weight': how much a shortage in the camp store (or nobody knowing of good places, for Scouts) counts as a need for the job, next to the society qualities. 'sole_provider_worth': what having someone keep an amenity nobody else keeps (the fire) is worth when weighing a move, in weighted quality points (the Fire quality follows people warming up, not the keeper, so leaders need this to keep a Firekeeper).
appoint._rank_comment: 'rank_weight': how much more an appointer likes moving someone up the hierarchy of work, per rank (they welcome it, society.json 'job_rank'); 'demote_weight': how much less they like moving someone down, per rank (they resent it). 'demote_gap_full': the reluctance to move someone down fades as the need for the work grows, gone once the gap reaches this (an empty store needs Gatherers whatever their pride). 'no_tool_reluctance': how much less they like appointing to work whose tools aren't in the camp store yet (the appointee would wait for one).

research._comment: Queuing research (anyone whose role covers the innovation's kind; it takes no time). Score: 'base' + 'curiosity' x their curiosity + 'opens' if it opens a job or government - its cost (against the game's price level) + 'empty_queue' while nothing is being researched + 'free' if it costs nothing. At most once every 'days_between' days each, and not while 'max_queue' are queued. 'cheapest_first' (the user's rule, 2026-11-16): an NPC considers only the cheapest innovation it could queue; the rest of the score decides whether it queues it now.
research._cost_scale_comment: An innovation costing this many points counts as one full step dearer when NPCs weigh what to research (costs are in each age's innovations.json).

dismiss._comment: Appointers dismiss someone from work only when their work quality is below 'poor_below'.

volunteer._comment: Taking up open work: +'need' x how short the tribe is of what the work provides, -'crowding' x the share of the tribe already doing it (there is no limit per job, so this spreads people out).

work._comment: Choosing work. 'luck_weight': how much a trip's chance of coming back with anything (work.json 'trips') counts (0 = ignore it, 1 = value a 40% trip at 40%). A Scout chooses what to look for by how short the tribe is of what trips to that kind of place bring back (no food: berry grounds, game trails or a fishing pool), times 'scout_known_factor' per 2 trips' worth already found and not yet used; never less than 'scout_need' (knowing where to go never hurts). Gatherers, Hunters and Fishers go for what is shortest, valuing a trip by its chance, which is certain while a found place has something left. 'store_share_of_target': food and water count as short when the camp store holds less than this share of work.json 'stock_targets' per member (the rest is in people's packs). 'content_weight': how much more an NPC wants to do their own job's work as their Work contentment falls below 'content_wanted' (it rises only while they work). 'own_need_weight': how much keener an NPC is on work that brings back food (or water) while they themselves are hungry (or thirsty). 'waiting_tool_need': how short the camp counts a tool that someone is waiting for (appointed to work they can't do without one; 1 = as short as can be). 'lesser_tool_factor': how keen a Toolmaker still is to make a tool while they could make a better one that stands in for it (items.json 'counts_as').

care._comment: 'critical_bonus': added to the urge to eat or drink once that need is below its 'critical' level (character.json), so a starving NPC eats before sleeping.

politics._comment: Whom an unhappy tribe moves against: the top office (most points) carries all the discontent with the leaders, a lesser office (its points / the top office's) ^ 'blame_exponent' of it. A holder doing their job badly is a grievance whatever the office.
politics._vacant_seat_comment: 'vacant_seat': how much an empty office seat (its holder died, say) counts like discontent toward campaigning for it by persuasion, x the office's blame share (the top office most). It needs no patience to run out.

health._comment: How NPCs look after their health (data/life.json). Someone ill does work and play only 'work_when_ill' as keenly (health comes back only while not working), someone below 'rest_below' health 'work_when_hurt' as keenly. Seeing the healer scores 'treat_when_ill' (plus up to 4 more the lower their health) when ill, else 'treat_when_hurt' x the share of health lost. A healer goes to heal someone ill with 'heal_ill' (plus up to 4 the lower their health), someone weak with 'heal_hurt' x the share of health lost: above any other work. While anyone is ill, crafting that uses up medicine (herbs into a poultice) is only 'craft_medicine_while_ill' as keen.

remains._comment: Laying the dead to rest (work.json tasks with 'disposes_of_dead'): it scores 'base' + 'per_body' per body lying in camp + 'per_year' per year the oldest has lain there, less 'own_work_weight' for someone with their own job's work to do and 'risk_weight' x the task's 'illness_risk' (so the safer way is preferred). Only one person goes for each body.

childhood._comment: NPC children play and study (data/life.json 'childhood') whenever their bodies allow: each activity scores 'base' + 'taste' x the child's own lasting liking for it (0-1, different for every child: it is what makes children grow up different) + 'bored_weight' x how low their Work contentment is, + up to 'noise'; x 'night_factor' at night.
